knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7)

# What this does

For every sonde site it builds a **flow-informed K600 prior** for
`streammetabolizer_updated.Rmd`, using published reach-scale equations:

1. **Flow**: daily discharge from USGS and Colorado DWR gauges (direct gauge where
   `flow_source` names one, otherwise a documented proxy; see `site_gauge_map.csv`).
2. **Slope and drainage area** from the site's lat/long, snapped to the NHDPlusV2
   flowline (`nhdplusTools`). You can override with a surveyed/LiDAR slope in
   `site_metadata.csv` (column `slope`).
3. **Velocity and depth** from discharge via a hydraulic geometry fitted to USGS field
   measurements at the nearby gauges (at-a-station power laws, V = a Q^b, D = c Q^f).
4. **k600** (m/d) from Raymond et al. (2012) Eq. 4, `k600 = 5037 (V S)^0.89 D^0.54`
   (also the model used to set priors for the NEON reaeration dataset, Aho et al. 2024),
   with Eq. 7 `4725 (V S)^0.86 Q^-0.14 D^0.66` as a sensitivity check.
   Both are in m/d with V in m/s, Q in m3/s, D in m.
5. **K600** (1/d) = k600 / depth. The site prior is the median of daily K600 over the
   days a sonde was deployed; the prior width is the day-to-day spread driven by flow.

Why a prior and not a "measured" K600: K600 is not identifiable from DO alone
(equifinality with ER; Appling et al. 2018). Priors from hydraulics are the
accepted way to constrain it when no tracer data exist (Hall & Ulseth 2020 review).

**Check before trusting numbers.** Steep reaches (energy dissipation above a threshold)
shift into a bubble-mediated regime where lowland-based equations can underestimate k600
by a large factor (Ulseth et al. 2019). The script flags those site-days (`eD`),
which matters for the upper Poudre sites (chd, pfal, pbr, sfm, joei, cbri, penn, lbea).

```{r libs}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("dataRetrieval", "nhdplusTools", "sf", "cdssr"))
# cdssr: remotes::install_github("anguswg-ucsb/cdssr")
# USGS API token (optional, avoids rate limits): put API_USGS_PAT in ~/.Renviron
```

# 1. Settings

```{r config}
DATA_DIR   <- "project/data"
META_FILE  <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "site_metadata.csv")
GAUGE_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "site_gauge_map.csv")
FLOW_DIR   <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "flow_manual")      # for Larimer County sites
OUT_DIR    <- "dashboard_data"; dir.create(OUT_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE)
START <- "2019-01-01"; END <- "2025-12-31"
CFS_TO_CMS <- 0.0283168
G <- 9.81
ED_HIGH <- 0.02            # m2 s-3; high-energy flag. CONFIRM the threshold in Ulseth et al. 2019
MIN_SDLOG <- 0.15          # floor on prior width (log scale)
K600_FALLBACK <- 30; SDLOG_FALLBACK <- 0.7   # ungauged / failed sites (wide prior)
HG_MIN_MEAS <- 8           # min field measurements to fit site hydraulic geometry
EXCLUDE_SITES <- c("pman", "penn", "lbea")   # dropped from the K600 calculations
```

# 2. Sites, gauges, slope and drainage area

```{r sites}
site_meta_all <- read_csv(META_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE)          # full file, rewritten untouched at the end
site_meta <- site_meta_all |> filter(!site %in% EXCLUDE_SITES)
gauges    <- read_csv(GAUGE_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE) |> filter(!site %in% EXCLUDE_SITES)
sites <- site_meta |> left_join(gauges, by = "site") |> filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon))

# snap each sonde to its NHDPlusV2 flowline, then pull slope and drainage area
# the attribute table is downloaded once (and cached) rather than once per site
vaa <- nhdplusTools::get_vaa(c("slope", "totdasqkm", "lengthkm")) |> mutate(comid = as.numeric(comid))

get_reach <- function(lat, lon) {
  pt <- sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(lon, lat)), crs = 4326)
  id <- as.numeric(nhdplusTools::discover_nhdplus_id(pt))
  if (length(id) != 1 || is.na(id)) stop("no NHDPlus flowline found at this point")
  out <- vaa |> filter(comid == id)
  if (!nrow(out)) stop("comid ", id, " is not in the VAA table")
  tibble(comid = id, nhd_slope = out$slope[1], da_km2 = out$totdasqkm[1], reach_km = out$lengthkm[1])
}

# run get_reach(sites$lat[1], sites$lon[1]) by hand first if this comes back empty: the error will print
reach <- pmap(list(sites$site, sites$lat, sites$lon), \(s, la, lo)
              tryCatch(get_reach(la, lo) |> mutate(site = s),
                       error = \(e) { message(s, ": ", conditionMessage(e)); NULL })) |>
  bind_rows()
stopifnot("No reaches found: see the messages above" = nrow(reach) > 0)

sites <- sites |> left_join(reach, by = "site") |>
  mutate(slope = coalesce(if ("slope" %in% names(sites)) slope else NA_real_, na_if(nhd_slope, -9998)))
sites |> select(site, comid, slope, da_km2, reach_km)
```

NHDPlusV2 slope is a coarse reach average; very short reaches or reservoirs give unreliable
values. Replace with a surveyed or LiDAR-derived slope (add a `slope` column to
`site_metadata.csv`) for any site where this table looks wrong.

# 3. Gauge flow (USGS + Colorado DWR + manual)

```{r flow}
usgs_ids <- gauges |> filter(source == "usgs") |> pull(gauge_id) |> unique()
dwr_ids  <- gauges |> filter(source == "dwr")  |> pull(gauge_id) |> unique()

# USGS: new Water Data API (read_waterdata_daily replaces readNWISdv)
flow_usgs <- dataRetrieval::read_waterdata_daily(
  monitoring_location_id = usgs_ids, parameter_code = "00060", statistic_id = "00003",
  time = paste0(START, "/", END)) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |> as_tibble() |>
  transmute(gauge_id = monitoring_location_id, date = as.Date(time), q_cfs = as.numeric(value),
            flow_estimated = qualifier != "", approval_status)   # unit_of_measure is ft^3/s

# Colorado DWR telemetry stations via CDSS REST
flow_dwr <- map(dwr_ids, \(id) cdssr::get_telemetry_ts(abbrev = id, parameter = "DISCHRG",
                  start_date = START, end_date = END, timescale = "day") |>
                  as_tibble() |> mutate(gauge_id = id)) |> bind_rows()
# the date/value column names differ between package versions: inspect names(flow_dwr)
flow_dwr <- flow_dwr |> transmute(gauge_id, date = as.Date(coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("meas_date", "measDate"), names(flow_dwr))))),
                                  q_cfs = as.numeric(coalesce(!!!syms(intersect(c("meas_value", "measValue", "value"), names(flow_dwr))))))

# Larimer County ALERT sites: one csv per gauge with columns date,q_cfs
flow_man <- list.files(FLOW_DIR, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) |>
  map(\(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(gauge_id = tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(f)), date = as.Date(date))) |>
  bind_rows()

flow_gauge <- bind_rows(flow_usgs, flow_dwr, flow_man) |>
  filter(!is.na(q_cfs)) |> mutate(q_cms = q_cfs * CFS_TO_CMS)

flow_gauge |> group_by(gauge_id) |>
  summarise(first = min(date), last = max(date), days = n(),
            q_min = min(q_cms), q_median = median(q_cms), q_max = max(q_cms))
```

Each gauge's record is plotted below so gaps and flow regimes are visible before anything is
computed from them.

```{r flow-plot}
ggplot(flow_gauge, aes(date, q_cms)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3, colour = "#33415C") +
  scale_y_log10() + facet_wrap(~ gauge_id, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Daily mean discharge at the reference gauges", x = NULL, y = expression(Q~(m^3~s^{-1}))) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 4. Site discharge

Direct gauges are used as is. For proxies, flow is optionally scaled by the drainage-area ratio
(`area_scale = TRUE`). This ignores diversions, canals and reservoir releases, which are
large on the Poudre, so proxy-based K600 values carry the lowest confidence.

```{r site-q}
gauge_da <- gauges |> filter(relation == "direct") |> select(gauge_id, site) |>
  left_join(sites |> select(site, da_gauge = da_km2), by = "site") |> distinct(gauge_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |> select(-site)

site_q <- sites |> filter(source != "none") |>
  select(site, gauge_id, relation, area_scale, da_km2) |>
  left_join(gauge_da, by = "gauge_id") |>
  mutate(scale = if_else(area_scale & !is.na(da_km2) & !is.na(da_gauge), da_km2 / da_gauge, 1)) |>
  left_join(flow_gauge, by = "gauge_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  transmute(site, date, relation, q_cms = q_cms * scale)
```

# 5. Hydraulic geometry from USGS channel measurements

Velocity and depth are not in the sonde files, so they are predicted from discharge using
power laws fitted to USGS streamflow measurements at the gauges. `read_waterdata_channel()`
returns discharge, width and area for each measurement, so velocity is `V = Q / A` and mean
depth is `D = A / W`. The fits are `V = a Q^b` and `D = c Q^f`. One regional fit is used for
all sites unless a site's own gauge has at least `HG_MIN_MEAS` measurements.

```{r hg}
ch <- dataRetrieval::read_waterdata_channel(monitoring_location_id = usgs_ids) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |> as_tibble()
glimpse(ch)                 # check the column names and units on first run
count(ch, channel_name)     # if a "Total" row exists next to sub-channel rows, filter to it below
```

```{r hg-fit}
HG_FROM <- as.Date("2000-01-01")   # channels change over decades; raise this if fits look noisy

to_si <- function(x, unit, ft_factor) ifelse(grepl("ft", unit, ignore.case = TRUE), x * ft_factor, x)

hg_meas <- ch |>
  filter(as.Date(time) >= HG_FROM, !is.na(channel_width), !is.na(channel_area)) |>   # drops old flow-only rows
  mutate(q_cms = to_si(channel_flow,  channel_flow_unit,  CFS_TO_CMS),
         w_m   = to_si(channel_width, channel_width_unit, 0.3048),
         a_m2  = to_si(channel_area,  channel_area_unit,  0.092903)) |>
  group_by(monitoring_location_id, field_visit_id, measurement_number, time) |>      # one row per measurement
  summarise(n_rows = n(), q_cms = sum(q_cms), w_m = sum(w_m), a_m2 = sum(a_m2), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(v_ms = q_cms / a_m2, d_m = a_m2 / w_m) |>
  filter(is.finite(v_ms), is.finite(d_m), q_cms > 0, v_ms > 0, d_m > 0)

# diagnostics: usable measurements per gauge, and whether any measurement had several channel rows
hg_meas |> group_by(monitoring_location_id) |>
  summarise(n = n(), first = min(as.Date(time)), last = max(as.Date(time)),
            multi_channel = sum(n_rows > 1), q_min = min(q_cms), q_max = max(q_cms))

fit_hg <- function(d) {
  mv <- lm(log(v_ms) ~ log(q_cms), d); md <- lm(log(d_m) ~ log(q_cms), d)
  tibble(a_v = exp(coef(mv)[1]), b_v = coef(mv)[2], c_d = exp(coef(md)[1]), f_d = coef(md)[2],
         n = nrow(d), r2_v = summary(mv)$r.squared, r2_d = summary(md)$r.squared)
}
hg_regional <- fit_hg(hg_meas)
hg_by_gauge <- hg_meas |> group_by(monitoring_location_id) |> filter(n() >= HG_MIN_MEAS) |> group_modify(~ fit_hg(.x))
list(regional = hg_regional, by_gauge = hg_by_gauge)
```

Sanity check: the velocity and depth exponents (`b_v`, `f_d`) should each be roughly 0.2 to 0.5,
with `r2` well above zero. Values far outside that range usually mean a units problem
or mixed total and sub-channel rows.

# 6. K600 from hydraulics

```{r k600}
hg_for <- function(site_id, gauge_id) {
  h <- hg_by_gauge |> filter(monitoring_location_id == gauge_id)
  if (nrow(h)) h else hg_regional
}

k600_daily <- site_q |>
  left_join(sites |> select(site, slope), by = "site") |>
  filter(!is.na(slope), slope > 0, q_cms > 0) |>
  mutate(
    V  = hg_regional$a_v * q_cms^hg_regional$b_v,
    D  = hg_regional$c_d * q_cms^hg_regional$f_d,
    eD = G * slope * V,                                            # energy dissipation, m2 s-3
    k600_eq4 = 5037 * (V * slope)^0.89 * D^0.54,                  # m/d, Raymond 2012 Eq. 4
    k600_eq7 = 4725 * (V * slope)^0.86 * q_cms^-0.14 * D^0.66,    # m/d, Raymond 2012 Eq. 7
    K600_eq4 = k600_eq4 / D, K600_eq7 = k600_eq7 / D,              # 1/d
    high_energy = eD > ED_HIGH)

# only days a sonde actually recorded dissolved oxygen
read_do_days <- function(f) read_csv(f, col_types = cols_only(DateTime_UTC = col_character(), site = col_character(),
                                      parameter = col_character(), value_final = col_double()), progress = FALSE) |>
  filter(parameter == "DO", !is.na(value_final)) |> transmute(site, date = as.Date(substr(DateTime_UTC, 1, 10))) |> distinct()
do_days <- list.files(DATA_DIR, "^CSU_ROSS_\\d{4}_cleaned\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE) |> map(read_do_days) |> bind_rows() |> distinct()

k600_deployed <- inner_join(k600_daily, do_days, by = c("site", "date"))
```

# 7. Site priors

```{r priors}
k600_priors <- k600_deployed |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(n_days = n(), flow_confidence = first(relation),
            q_median_cms = median(q_cms), q_p10 = quantile(q_cms, .1), q_p90 = quantile(q_cms, .9),
            slope = first(slope), pct_high_energy = round(100 * mean(high_energy)),
            K600_prior   = median(K600_eq4),
            K600_p10     = quantile(K600_eq4, .1), K600_p90 = quantile(K600_eq4, .9),
            K600_sdlog   = pmax(sd(log(K600_eq4)), MIN_SDLOG),
            K600_eq7_median = median(K600_eq7), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(K600_eq4_vs_eq7 = round(K600_prior / K600_eq7_median, 2))

# sites with no gauge or slope get the wide fallback
missing <- setdiff(site_meta$site, k600_priors$site)
k600_priors <- bind_rows(k600_priors, tibble(site = missing, flow_confidence = "none",
                                             K600_prior = K600_FALLBACK, K600_sdlog = SDLOG_FALLBACK))
# Manual, assumption-based priors for sites without usable flow (see k600_manual_overrides.csv).
# These replace computed or fallback values and are labelled "manual assumption".
MANUAL_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "k600_manual_overrides.csv")
if (file.exists(MANUAL_FILE)) {
  manual <- read_csv(MANUAL_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE)
  k600_priors <- k600_priors |>
    rows_upsert(manual |> transmute(site, K600_prior, K600_sdlog, flow_confidence = "manual assumption"), by = "site")
}

k600_priors |> arrange(match(site, site_meta$site))
```

Read this table before using it. If `pct_high_energy` is large, the Raymond equations are being
applied outside the conditions they were fitted for. If `K600_eq4_vs_eq7` is far from 1, the two
equations disagree and the prior is poorly constrained, so widen `K600_sdlog`.

```{r plots, fig.height=9}
k600_deployed |>
  mutate(site = factor(site, levels = site_meta$site, labels = site_meta$site_label)) |>
  ggplot(aes(q_cms, K600_eq4, colour = high_energy)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.7) + scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#33415C", `TRUE` = "#C0562B"), name = "eD above threshold") +
  facet_wrap(~ site, ncol = 4, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Flow-driven K600 on days with sonde data", x = expression(Q~(m^3~s^{-1})), y = expression(K[600]~(d^{-1}))) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

# 8. Write back to the metadata and export

```{r export}
site_meta_k <- site_meta_all |>
  select(-any_of(c("K600_prior", "K600_sdlog"))) |>
  left_join(k600_priors |> select(site, K600_prior, K600_sdlog, flow_confidence), by = "site")
write_csv(site_meta_k, file.path(DATA_DIR, "site_metadata.csv"))   # read by streammetabolizer_updated.Rmd
write_csv(k600_priors,  file.path(OUT_DIR, "k600_site_priors.csv"))
write_csv(k600_deployed |> select(site, date, q_cms, V, D, slope, eD, high_energy, K600_eq4, K600_eq7),
          file.path(OUT_DIR, "k600_daily_by_site.csv"))
write_csv(flow_gauge, file.path(OUT_DIR, "gauge_daily_flow.csv"))
```

The last file is the flow series for the dashboard's flow overlay (`gauge_daily_flow.csv`
joined to sites through `site_gauge_map.csv`).
